children: The Rs 3.87 crore project is expected to meet more than 90 per cent of Aster Medcity’s energy needs and offset around 23,138 tonnes of CO₂ emissions annually

Aster DM Quality Care has commissioned a 10 MW solar power project for Aster Medcity in Kerala in partnership with Oyster Renewable Energy, investing Rs 3.87 crore in the project. The facility is expected to generate 16-17.5 million units of renewable energy annually and meet more than 90 per cent of the hospital’s total energy requirement on a captive basis.

Developed by Oyster Renewable, the ground-mounted solar project is located at Ambalathara and adjoining villages in Hosdurg Taluka, Kasargod district. It uses bifacial solar modules designed for Kerala’s tropical climate and is intended to provide reliable renewable power for the hospital’s round-the-clock operations.

The power will be supplied through Oyster Green Hybrid Two Private Ltd, in which the Aster Group holds a 26 per cent equity stake. The project is being commissioned in phases, with the current milestone marking its first operational phase and full commissioning expected in subsequent stages.

Once fully operational, the project is expected to offset approximately 23,138 metric tonnes of CO₂ emissions annually, reducing the carbon footprint associated with Aster Medcity’s energy consumption. Ramesh Kumar, CEO (India 1), Aster DM Quality Care, said, “Integrating renewable energy into our operations is an important part of our commitment to building a more sustainable healthcare ecosystem. This 10 MW solar project for Aster Medcity will not only help meet a significant proportion of the hospital's energy requirements through clean power but also strengthen our efforts towards reducing the environmental footprint of our operations.”

Siddharth Bhatia, Managing Director & CEO, Oyster Renewable Energy, said the project was the company’s second-largest solar installation for a healthcare institution to date. “Healthcare facilities demand uninterrupted, reliable power, and this project has been engineered to meet exactly that standard,” he said. Bhatia added that the project’s expected annual carbon abatement of around 23,138 tonnes would contribute to Kerala’s sustainability goals and India’s broader clean-energy transition.

The project comes as healthcare providers increasingly explore renewable energy to manage the high and continuous power requirements of hospitals while reducing dependence on grid-based fossil-fuel electricity. For Aster Medcity, the solar installation is expected to combine energy security with lower environmental impact as the group expands its sustainability initiatives across healthcare infrastructure.
